Bird flu spread quickly through Central Washington dairy farms in October, with 40 Washington herds testing positive from Oct. 7 to Oct. 30, according to the U.S. Department of Agriculture; 33 were in Yakima County and one was in neighboring Benton County. Officials confirmed the first two cases at Yakima County dairies on Oct. 8 and four additional cases on Oct. 29. A Yakima County resident exposed to infected dairy cattle died Nov. 1, and local officials also reported two other human infections linked to cattle. Containing the virus is difficult because cattle farms cannot be sealed and controlled as tightly as poultry barns, said Rick Naerbout, executive director of the Washington State Dairy Federation. The federation advised farmers on Oct. 4 to follow biosecurity plans and alert veterinarians to falling milk production; researchers have not established the virus’s natural route of spread among cows. Washington officials say infected cows generally recover within four to six weeks, and state agriculture officials say pasteurized milk remains safe.

items.title: [phys.org] Researchers document sustained sexual bond between Ethiopian bull and male donkey
items.content_html:
🌾 ✏️

An Italian-led research team documented repeated sexual interactions between a bull and a male donkey on an Ethiopian plateau, describing a selective social bond between the animals. During eight days of observation in March 2026, the bull, Achilles, mounted the donkey, Patroclus, 51 times; 34 mountings involved penetration. The findings appeared Nov. 2 in the journal Current Biology. The pair also licked, rubbed and nuzzled one another, and researchers repeatedly saw them seek each other out despite access to other potential mates. The team cautions that observations of one domesticated pair cannot establish why the behavior occurred or what the animals felt. Dry-season conditions led herders to move them to separate pastures; researchers in Ethiopia are trying to arrange a reunion to observe whether their interactions resume.

items.title: [farms.com] Livestock reports highlight forage planning amid drought and feed-supply concerns
items.content_html:
🌾 ✏️

Livestock guidance published across the United States, France and Poland focuses on forage stocks, grazing and feed transitions during drought and uneven feed supplies. In France, independent livestock nutrition consultant Eva Garre urged farmers to measure silage and hay reserves, account for losses of 15% to 30% and calculate shortages by date; early maize samples showed starch levels of 18 to 20 points, compared with the usual 34 to 37 in her region. Kenny Simon, an extension forages instructor at the University of Arkansas Division of Agriculture, recommended rotational grazing, moving hay-feeding sites and planting winter annuals to reduce stress on dry pastures. A Polish cattle farm keeps cows and calves on about 100 hectares of pasture from May through November and produces its own hay and silage. South Dakota State University Extension feedlot specialist Warren Rusche advised keeping newly arrived calves in smaller feedlot pens for their first three weeks and feeding them twice daily during the initial adjustment. Argentine feedlot analyst Andrés Halle cautioned that theoretical feedlot margins can misstate results when current grain prices are applied to grain produced on-farm.

Carbon dioxide averaged 426.8 parts per million, methane 1,948 parts per billion and nitrous oxide 339.1 parts per billion—153%, 267% and 126% of pre-industrial levels, respectively. The annual bulletin measures gases accumulated in the atmosphere, not emissions released during the year. About half of annual carbon dioxide emissions remain in the atmosphere. The WMO says the gases’ heat-trapping effect will drive warming for decades or centuries; the past 11 years were the warmest on record. Carbon dioxide rose 2.8 parts per million from 2024 to 2025, below the previous year’s 3.6-ppm increase but still above the decade average of 2.6 ppm. The WMO linked the slower increase partly to recovering land carbon sinks and fewer fire emissions after the 2023-24 El Niño. It warned that concentrations could rise further in 2026 as fossil-fuel use continues and another powerful El Niño affects land sinks. The bulletin will inform negotiators at the Nov. 9-20 COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Türkiye.

European Central Bank policymakers held the deposit rate at 2.5% on Oct. 29, but President Christine Lagarde said they had seriously discussed a rate increase as energy prices and bond yields tightened financing conditions for households and businesses. Eurozone inflation reached 3.8% in September, and average 10-year government bond yields had risen about 35 basis points since the ECB’s September forecast. France’s 10-year borrowing cost topped 5% last week for the first time since 2002. The same day, Lagarde said she would leave the Frankfurt-based central bank on Feb. 7, 2027, before the end of her eight-year term, saying she wanted to speak on issues beyond monetary policy. Her departure opens a contest to lead the institution that sets interest rates across the euro area. Markets showed little reaction to the announcement, with analysts saying the ECB’s established practices were likely to outlast its president. Investors were pricing in three further rate increases by the end of 2027, which would bring the deposit rate to 3.25%. The ECB’s next policy meeting is scheduled for Dec. 17.

items.title: [theguardian.com] China expels 33 senior officials as Xi tightens party discipline
items.content_html:

China’s ruling Communist Party expelled 33 senior officials at the close of a four-day leadership meeting in Beijing on Oct. 29, confirming the removal of former senior military commander Zhang Youxia, former Xinjiang party chief Ma Xingrui and others. Sixteen of those expelled were from the military. The party’s communiqué cited serious disciplinary and legal violations without detailing individual allegations. Only 279 of the 376 full and alternate Central Committee members appointed in 2022 attended — the lowest attendance at a plenum under President Xi Jinping, with a record number of empty seats. Purges have reduced the seven-member Central Military Commission, which commands China’s armed forces, to Xi and General Zhang Shengmin, a military anti-corruption official. The party promoted Zhang Shengmin to the Politburo at the meeting. The meeting focused on internal discipline and anti-corruption, while analysts differ on whether the drive chiefly addresses graft or reinforces Xi’s authority. The party also confirmed that its 21st congress will take place in Beijing in the second half of 2027, when it will reshuffle its leadership and Xi is widely expected to seek a fourth term.

Marvell Technology announced Nov. 2 that it would acquire Lumentum in an all-stock deal, combining its custom silicon and networking equipment with Lumentum’s lasers and other optical components. The companies aim to address a growing AI data-center constraint: copper links struggle to keep pace as large clusters move data among thousands of processors. Optical links can carry data between chips at speeds and distances that copper wiring cannot sustain, according to the companies and industry reporting. Marvell says combining electrical and optical technologies would let it design a wider range of connectivity products. Lumentum also brings optical circuit switching and specialized manufacturing capabilities. The companies say the transaction requires shareholder and regulatory approval and expect it to close in the first half of 2028.

The Houthis renewed their warning to airlines, airport staff and passengers, calling the airport a military target.

items.title: [newsletter.pragmaticengineer.com] AI coding tools reshape software jobs as junior hiring and enrollment fall
items.content_html:
🌾 ✏️

AI coding agents are shifting software development from writing code to directing models, reviewing their output and making architectural decisions, as companies use the tools to produce more of their software. U.S. undergraduate enrollment in computer science dropped more than 12% this fall, while graduate enrollment fell more than 10%. Employment among software developers aged 22 to 25 has fallen about 20% since late 2022, according to studies cited by Bloomberg and t3n. Companies may need fewer junior developers for routine coding, but experienced engineers still make decisions about security, code quality and system design — skills often learned through early-career work. Critical Software co-founder Gonçalo Quadros said the company is reorganizing around AI while keeping people responsible for design and validation in aviation, aerospace and automotive systems. He estimated AI could let it build technology ten times faster.
